title: The Siege of the Randhawa Village

blocks.text: The betrayal becomes public when the informer reported about the Singhs assembly to the neighbouring Jats, turning private knowledge into the opening move of a coordinated assault.

Soon the Mughal troops laid a siege to the village so tightly that not even a dog could escape through the siege, making survival depend less on strength than on the mercy of encircling enemies who had none.

The massacre that follows is remembered through the arrest and killing of elders, especially by laying their hands on the fourteen Sikh elders, after which the page asks in grief whether anybody survived this ordeal out of their progeny.
